subject: Geopolitics
title: Lessons from Intelligence Failures
description: A quick, practical guide to Lessons from Intelligence Failures.

hook.text: Every major intelligence failure has the same root cause: humans see what they expect to see, not what is there.

buildup.text: Cognitive biases infect analysis. Confirmation bias, mirror imaging, and anchoring distort even the best data.

discovery.text: Red teams — groups assigned to challenge assumptions — help.

twist.text: Reforms follow every failure. New agencies are created, then slowly develop the same blind spots as the old ones.

climax.text: Perfect intelligence is impossible. The goal is reducing surprise without creating paralysis through over-analysis.

punchline.text: The failure is never the last one. The lesson always needs relearning.

quiz.question: What is the most common root cause of intelligence failures?
options: Lack of funding for intelligence agencies
Cognitive biases that make analysts see what they expect
